title: Multiple Large Tumefactive MS Plaques in a Young Man: A Diagnostic Enigma and Therapeutic Challenge
case_prompt:
An 18-year-old man was referred with a 6-day history of progressive neurologic symptoms and an abnormal brain MRI. He initially noted weakness and paresthesia of the right upper extremity that gradually extended to the left arm and both lower limbs. On day 3, he experienced haziness of vision in the right eye with pain on lateral gaze and several generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

On examination he was alert and afebrile. Neurologic findings included right visual acuity of 20/200 with a central scotoma and papillitis on fundoscopy, jerk nystagmus on lateral gaze, decreased muscle strength (right 3/5, left 4/5), +1 deep-tendon reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, and a mild ataxic gait with intact sensation. He was started on valproate.

Laboratory studies showed normal CBC, blood glucose, electrolytes, liver and kidney function tests, and urinalysis; ESR was 15 mm/h. Serologic tests for HIV, HCV, EBV, HZV, Borrelia, and Toxoplasma were negative; tuberculosis skin test and collagen-vascular workup were negative; chest radiograph was normal. Cerebrospinal fluid had 2 RBCs, 0 WBCs, protein 125 mg/dL, glucose 50 mg/dL (serum 110 mg/dL), LDH 43 U/mL, and positive oligoclonal bands. Visual-evoked potentials in the right eye and left-sided sensory-evoked potentials were prolonged. Cervical spine MRI was normal.

Brain MRI demonstrated multiple large, round lesions in the right centrum semiovale and periventricular left occipital region extending to the splenium of the corpus callosum. These had central T1 hypointensity, T2 hyperintensity, peripheral T2 hypointense rims, associated severe vasogenic edema, heterogeneous postcontrast enhancement, but no mass effect or midline shift.

Differential diagnoses included acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, multifocal glioma, metastasis, vasculitis, lymphoma, lymphoproliferative disease, and tumefactive multiple sclerosis. A stereotactic brain biopsy was recommended but was refused by the patient and his family.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis was considered — “These findings brought several differential diagnoses such as acute disseminated encephalomyelitis… under consideration.”  
2. Multifocal glioma was considered — “…differential diagnoses such as… multifocal glioma… under consideration.”  
3. Metastasis was considered — “…differential diagnoses such as… metastasis… under consideration.”  
4. Vasculitis was considered — “…differential diagnoses such as… vasculitis… under consideration.”  
5. Lymphoma was considered — “…differential diagnoses such as… lymphoma… under consideration.”  
6. Lymphoproliferative diseases were considered — “…differential diagnoses such as… lymphoproliferative diseases… under consideration.”  
7. Tumefactive multiple sclerosis was favored given supportive inflammatory and demyelinating features — “This decision was made on the basis of the presence of papillitis, normal blood tests, prolonged VEP and SEP, presence of OCB, and no shift in midline structure in spite of large lesions.”
